sentences.zh: 泉企 李遷哲 楊乾運 扶猛 陽雄 席固 任果

translations.literal: Quan Qi; Li Qianzhe; Yang Ganyun; Fu Meng; Yang Xiong; Xi Gu; Ren Guo
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Quan Qi, Li Qianzhe, Yang Ganyun, Fu Meng, Yang Xiong, Xi Gu, and Ren Guo

sentences.zh: 泉企字思道，上洛豐陽人也。

translations.literal: Quan Qi, courtesy name Sidao, was a native of Fengyang in Shangluo.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Qi, whose courtesy name was Sidao, came from Fengyang in Shangluo commandery.

sentences.zh: 世雄商洛。

translations.literal: For generations his clan had been powerful in Shang and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long been dominant in the Shangluo region.

sentences.zh: 曾祖景言，魏建節將軍，假宜陽郡守，世襲本縣令，封丹水侯。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Jingyan was a Jianjie General of Wei, acting Administrator of Yiyang Commandery, hereditary Magistrate of the home county, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Danshui.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Jingyan had served Wei as a jianjie general and acting administrator of Yiyang, held the hereditary magistracy of their home county, and been enfeoffed as marquis of Danshui.

sentences.zh: 父安志，復為建節將軍、宜陽郡守，領本縣令，降爵為伯。

translations.literal: His father Anzhi again served as Jianjie General and Administrator of Yiyang Commandery, concurrently holding the home county magistracy, with his noble rank reduced to baron.
translations.idiomatic: His father Anzhi likewise became a jianjie general and administrator of Yiyang while continuing as magistrate of their county, though his title was reduced to baron.

sentences.zh: 企九歲喪父，哀毀類於成人。

translations.literal: Qi at age nine lost his father; his grief and self-mortification were like those of an adult.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was only nine when his father died, yet his mourning was as deep as a grown man's.

sentences.zh: 服闋襲爵。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended he succeeded to the noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended, he inherited the family title.

sentences.zh: 年十二，鄉人皇平、陳合等三百餘人詣州請企為縣令。

translations.literal: At age twelve, more than three hundred fellow townsmen including Huang Ping and Chen He went to the province to request that Qi be made county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve, over three hundred local men led by Huang Ping and Chen He petitioned the provincial authorities to appoint Qi magistrate of the county.

sentences.zh: 州為申上，時吏部尚書郭祚以企年少，未堪宰民，請別選遣，終此一限，令企代之。

translations.literal: The province reported upward; at the time the Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Guo Zuo, because Qi was young and not yet fit to govern the people, requested that another be chosen and sent, to serve out this one term, after which Qi would replace him.
translations.idiomatic: The province forwarded the petition, but Guo Zuo, minister of personnel, argued that Qi was too young to govern and asked that someone else serve one term before Qi took office.

sentences.zh: 魏宣武帝詔曰：「企向成立，且為本鄉所樂，何為捨此世襲，更求一限。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu of Wei decreed: "Qi is already coming of age, and moreover is beloved by his home district—why abandon this hereditary office and seek another term?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu of Wei replied, "Qi is nearly grown, and his own district wants him—why set aside a hereditary post and insist on a substitute term?

sentences.zh: 」遂依所請。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the original request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then approved the original request.

sentences.zh: 企雖童幼，而好學恬靜，百姓安之。

translations.literal: Although Qi was still a child, he loved learning and was calm and quiet, and the common people were at ease under him.
translations.idiomatic: Though still a boy, Qi loved study and kept a quiet manner, and the people were content under his rule.

sentences.zh: 尋以母憂去職。

translations.literal: Soon he left office on account of mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He soon left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 縣中父老復表請殷勤，詔許之。

translations.literal: The elders of the county again submitted a petition with great earnestness, and an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The county elders petitioned again with great urgency, and the throne consented.

sentences.zh: 起復本任，加討寇將軍。

translations.literal: He was recalled to his former post and additionally made General Who Punishes Bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to his former post and given the additional rank of general who punishes bandits.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，又加龍驤將軍、假節、防洛州別將，尋除上洛郡守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang he was further made General of the Dragon Cavalry, given provisional credentials, and made deputy commander for the defense of Luo Province; soon he was appointed Administrator of Shangluo Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiaochang era he was made general of the dragon cavalry, given provisional credentials, and appointed deputy commander for Luo's defense, and soon became administrator of Shangluo.

sentences.zh: 及蕭寶夤反，遣其黨郭子恢襲據潼關。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin rebelled, he sent his partisan Guo Zihui to raid and seize Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Baoyin rose in rebellion, he sent his follower Guo Zihui to seize Tong Pass by surprise.

sentences.zh: 企率鄉兵三千人拒之，連戰數日，子弟死者二十許人，遂大破子恢。

translations.literal: Qi led three thousand local troops to resist him; after fighting several days in succession, about twenty of his sons and younger kinsmen died, yet he utterly defeated Zihui.
translations.idiomatic: Qi led three thousand local troops against him; after several days of fighting, nearly twenty of his sons and kinsmen fell, yet he routed Zihui completely.

sentences.zh: 以功拜征虜將軍。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed General Who Conquers the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was made general who conquers the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 寶夤又遣兵萬人趣青泥，誘動巴人，圖取上洛。

translations.literal: Baoyin again sent ten thousand troops toward Qingni, inciting the Ba people and plotting to take Shangluo.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin then sent ten thousand men toward Qingni, stirring up the Ba tribes in a bid to capture Shangluo.

sentences.zh: 上洛豪族泉、杜二姓密應之。

translations.literal: The powerful clans of the Quan and Du surnames in Shangluo secretly responded to him.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful Quan and Du clans of Shangluo secretly went over to him.

sentences.zh: 企與刺史董紹宗潛兵掩襲，二姓散走，寶夤軍亦退。

translations.literal: Qi and the Regional Inspector Dong Shaozong moved troops in secret for a surprise attack; the two clans scattered and fled, and Baoyin's army also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Qi and regional inspector Dong Shaozong struck by surprise with hidden troops; the two clans fled, and Baoyin's army withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 遷左將軍、淅州刺史，別封涇陽縣伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left General and Regional Inspector of Xi Province, separately enfeoffed as Baron of Jingyang County with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left general and inspector of Xi, and separately enfeoffed as baron of Jingyang with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 永安中，梁將王玄真入寇荊州。

translations.literal: In the Yongan era, the Liang general Wang Xuanzhen invaded Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongan, the Liang general Wang Xuanzhen raided Jing province.

sentences.zh: 加企持節、都督，率衆援之。

translations.literal: Qi was given credentials and made area commander, and led troops to reinforce it.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was given credentials and overall command and marched to relieve the province.

sentences.zh: 遇玄真于順陽，與戰，大破之。

translations.literal: He encountered Xuanzhen at Shunyang, fought him, and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He met Xuanzhen at Shunyang, gave battle, and routed him.

sentences.zh: 除撫軍將軍、使持節，假鎮南將軍、東雍州刺史，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: He was appointed Pacification Army General and Envoy Holding Credentials, acting General Who Guards the South and Regional Inspector of Eastern Yong Province, and his noble rank was advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He was made pacification army general with envoy credentials, acting general who guards the south and inspector of eastern Yong, and raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 部民楊羊皮，太保椿之從弟，恃托椿勢，侵害百姓。

translations.literal: A subject of his district, Yang Yangpi, a younger cousin of the Grand Guardian Chun, relied on Chun's power and oppressed the common people.
translations.idiomatic: A local man named Yang Yangpi, a cousin of Grand Guardian Yang Chun, used Chun's influence to bully the people.

sentences.zh: 守宰多被其淩侮，皆畏而不敢言。

translations.literal: Many local officials were insulted and humiliated by him; all feared him and did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: Many local officials suffered his abuse but were too afraid to complain.

sentences.zh: 企收而治之，將加極法，於是楊氏慚懼，宗族詣閤請恩。

translations.literal: Qi arrested and prosecuted him and was about to apply the extreme penalty; thereupon the Yang clan felt shame and fear, and the clan kindred came to the gate to beg grace.
translations.idiomatic: Qi arrested and tried him and was about to impose the death penalty; the Yang clan, shamed and terrified, came to his gate to plead for mercy.

sentences.zh: 自此豪右屏迹，無敢犯者。

translations.literal: From this time the powerful gentry kept out of sight, and none dared offend.
translations.idiomatic: After that the local bullies vanished, and none dared transgress again.

sentences.zh: 性又清約，纖毫不擾於民。

translations.literal: His nature was also frugal and restrained; not the slightest thing did he disturb among the people.
translations.idiomatic: He was also frugal by nature and never imposed the least burden on the people.

sentences.zh: 在州五年，每于鄉里運米以自給。

translations.literal: During five years in the province, each time he transported rice from his home district to supply himself.
translations.idiomatic: For five years in office he hauled his own grain from home rather than live off the province.

sentences.zh: 梁魏興郡與洛州接壤，表請與屬。

translations.literal: Liang's Weixing Commandery bordered Luo Province and submitted a memorial requesting to be placed under its jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's Weixing commandery, which bordered Luo, petitioned to be placed under Qi's jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 詔企為行臺尚書以撫納之。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Qi Mobile-Staff Director of the Secretariat to pacify and receive them.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Qi to serve as mobile-staff director of the secretariat to bring the district in.

sentences.zh: 大行臺賀拔岳以企昔蒞東雍，為吏民所懷，乃表企復為刺史，詔許之。

translations.literal: The Grand Mobile-Staff Director Heba Yue, because Qi had formerly governed Eastern Yong and was cherished by officials and people, memorialized that Qi again be made regional inspector, and an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand mobile-staff director Heba Yue, remembering how beloved Qi had been as governor of eastern Yong, recommended him for the post again, and the throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 蜀民張國雋聚黨剽刼，州郡不能制，企命收而戮之，闔境清肅。

translations.literal: The Shu native Zhang Guojun gathered a band for plunder and robbery; the province and commanderies could not control him; Qi ordered him seized and executed, and the whole territory became clear and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: A Shu man named Zhang Guojun led a band of raiders whom the local authorities could not suppress; Qi had him arrested and executed, and the whole region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武初，加車騎

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei, he was additionally made General of Chariots and
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowu's reign, he was promoted to general of chariots and

translations.literal: (Da) (emended: Great)
translations.idiomatic: (Da) (emended: great)

sentences.zh: 將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Cavalry and Left Grand Master for Glorious Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: cavalry and left grand master for glorious affairs.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武專政，魏帝有西顧之心，欲委企以山南之事，乃除洛州刺史、當州都督。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan of Northern Qi monopolized government, the Emperor of Wei turned his thoughts westward and wished to entrust Qi with affairs south of the mountains; thereupon he was appointed Regional Inspector of Luo Province and area commander of that province.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan seized power in the east, the Wei emperor looked west and meant to entrust the mountain south to Qi, appointing him inspector of Luo and commander of the province.

sentences.zh: 未幾，帝西遷，齊神武率衆至潼關，企遣其子元禮督鄉里五千人，北出大谷以禦之。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor moved west; Gao Huan led troops to Tong Pass; Qi sent his son Yuanli to command five thousand local men, marching north out of Dagu Valley to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the emperor fled west; Gao Huan advanced on Tong Pass, and Qi sent his son Yuanli at the head of five thousand local troops north through Dagu Valley to block him.

sentences.zh: 齊神武不敢進。

translations.literal: Gao Huan did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan did not dare press forward.

sentences.zh: 上洛人都督泉岳、其弟猛略與

translations.literal: Quan Yue, area commander of Shangluo, and his younger brother Menglue, together with
translations.idiomatic: Quan Yue, area commander of Shangluo, his younger brother Menglue, and

translations.literal: (Shun) (variant)
translations.idiomatic: (Shun) (variant reading)

sentences.zh: 〔拒〕陽人杜窋等謀翻洛州，以應東軍。

translations.literal: 〔Ju〕 Yang native Du Qiong and others plotted to turn Luo Province, to respond to the Eastern army.
translations.idiomatic: the men of Juyang, including Du Qiong, plotted to defect with Luo province and join the eastern forces.

sentences.zh: 企知之，殺岳及猛略等，傳首詣闕，而窋亡投東魏。

translations.literal: Qi learned of it, killed Yue and Menglue and the rest, sent their heads to the capital, while Qiong fled and went over to Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Qi learned of the plot, executed Yue and Menglue and their fellows, and sent their heads to court; Qiong alone escaped to Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 錄前後勳，授車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Recording his earlier and later achievements, he was given Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: For his accumulated service he was made grand general of chariots and cavalry with ceremonial parity to the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 大統初，加開府儀同三司，兼尚書右僕射，進爵上洛郡公，增邑通前千戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong he was additionally made Baron with an Establishment Equal to the Three Dukes, concurrently Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, advanced in rank to Duke of Shangluo Commandery, with fief households increased together with earlier holdings to one thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Datong he received an open office equal to the three dukes, served concurrently as right vice director of the secretariat, was raised to duke of Shangluo, and his fief was increased to one thousand households in all.

sentences.zh: 企志尚廉慎，每除一官，憂見顏色。

translations.literal: Qi's aims prized integrity and caution; each time he received a new office, worry showed on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Qi valued integrity and caution; every new appointment showed plainly on his face as worry.

sentences.zh: 至是頻讓，魏帝手詔不許。

translations.literal: At this time he repeatedly declined, but the Emperor of Wei's handwritten edict would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He now declined repeatedly, but the emperor's own edict refused his resignation.

sentences.zh: 三年，高敖曹率衆圍逼州城，杜窋為其鄉導。

translations.literal: In the third year, Gao Aocao led troops to surround and press the provincial city; Du Qiong served as their local guide.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Gao Aocao besieged the provincial capital, with Du Qiong guiding his forces through the countryside.

sentences.zh: 企拒守旬餘，矢盡援絕，城乃陷焉。

translations.literal: Qi resisted and defended for more than ten days; arrows were exhausted and reinforcements cut off, and the city then fell.
translations.idiomatic: Qi held out for more than ten days, but when arrows ran out and relief failed to come, the city fell.

sentences.zh: 企謂敖曹曰：「泉企力屈，志不服也。

translations.literal: Qi said to Aocao: "Quan Qi's strength is spent, but his will is not subdued.
translations.idiomatic: Qi told Aocao, "Quan Qi's strength is broken, but his will is not.

sentences.zh: 」及竇泰被擒，敖曹退走，遂執企而東，以窋為刺史。

translations.literal: " When Dou Tai was captured, Aocao withdrew and fled; he then seized Qi and took him east, making Qiong regional inspector.
translations.idiomatic: " When Dou Tai was captured, Aocao withdrew, seized Qi, and marched east, installing Qiong as governor.

sentences.zh: 企臨發，密誡子元禮、仲遵曰：「吾生平志願，不過令長耳。

translations.literal: As Qi was about to depart, he secretly admonished his sons Yuanli and Zhongzun: "In my life's ambitions, nothing more than magistrate and chief.
translations.idiomatic: Before he left, Qi secretly told his sons Yuanli and Zhongzun, "All my life I wanted nothing more than to be a county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 幸逢聖運，位亞台司。

translations.literal: Fortunately I met a sage age, and my position stood next to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: By good fortune I lived in a great age and rose nearly to the rank of the three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 今爵祿旣隆，年齒又暮，前途夷險，抑亦可知。

translations.literal: Now rank and salary are already lofty, and my years are also advanced; whether the road ahead is level or perilous may likewise be known.
translations.idiomatic: Now my titles and stipend are high and my years are many; whether what lies ahead is smooth or hard, you can already guess.

sentences.zh: 汝等志業方強，堪立功效。

translations.literal: You are in the prime of your ambitions and careers and are fit to establish merit.
translations.idiomatic: You are young and capable of real achievement.

sentences.zh: 且忠孝之道，不可兩全，宜各為身計，勿相隨寇手。

translations.literal: Moreover the way of loyalty and filial piety cannot be fully fulfilled in both; you should each plan for yourselves and not follow the enemy's hand.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty and filial duty cannot both be satisfied—each of you must look to his own course and not follow me into the enemy's hands.

sentences.zh: 但得汝等致力本朝，吾無餘恨。

translations.literal: If only you will devote your strength to the dynasty, I have no remaining regret.
translations.idiomatic: If you serve the dynasty with all your strength, I shall have no regret left.

sentences.zh: 不得以我在東，遂虧臣節也。

translations.literal: You must not because I am in the east then fall short in your ministerial integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Do not let the fact that I am in the east weaken your loyalty as subjects.

sentences.zh: 爾其勉之！

translations.literal: You must exert yourselves!
translations.idiomatic: Do your utmost!

sentences.zh: 」乃揮涕而訣，餘無所言，聞者莫不憤歎。

translations.literal: " He then waved away tears and took leave; beyond that he said nothing, and those who heard were none who did not burn with grief and sigh.
translations.idiomatic: " With that he brushed away his tears and said farewell; he spoke no more, and all who heard him were moved to grief and indignation.

sentences.zh: 尋卒於鄴。

translations.literal: Soon he died at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died at Ye.

sentences.zh: 元禮少有志氣，好弓馬，頗閑草隸，有士君子之風。

translations.literal: Yuanli in youth had ambition and spirit, loved bow and horse, was quite skilled in clerical and standard script, and had the bearing of a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli was ambitious from youth, loved archery and horsemanship, wrote a fair hand in clerical and standard scripts, and bore himself like a true gentleman.

sentences.zh: 釋褐奉朝請、本州別駕。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the russet he became Court Gentleman for the Imperial Audience and Vice Director of his home province.
translations.idiomatic: On entering service he became a court gentleman for imperial audience and vice director of his home province.

sentences.zh: 累遷員外散騎侍郎、洛州大中正、員外散騎常侍、安東將軍、持節、都督，賜爵臨洮縣伯，進征東將軍、金紫光祿大夫，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Supernumerary Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, chief rectifier of Luo Province, supernumerary regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, General Who Pacifies the East, credential-holder, and area commander; he was granted the noble rank Baron of Lintao County, advanced to General Who Campaigns East and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Radiance, and additionally made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through a series of posts—supernumerary attendant of the scattered cavalry, chief rectifier of Luo, supernumerary regular attendant, general who pacifies the east with credentials and overall command—and was enfeoffed baron of Lintao, then promoted to general who campaigns east and grand master of the golden seal and purple radiance, with the added rank of regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 及洛州陷，與企俱被執而東。

translations.literal: When Luo Province fell, together with Qi he was seized and taken east.
translations.idiomatic: When Luo fell, he was captured with his father and taken east.

sentences.zh: 元禮於路逃歸。

translations.literal: Yuanli on the road escaped and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli escaped on the road and made his way back.

sentences.zh: 時杜窋雖為刺史，然巴人素輕杜而重泉。

translations.literal: At the time although Du Qiong was regional inspector, the Ba people had always looked lightly on the Du and heavily on the Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Though Du Qiong now held the governorship, the Ba people had always respected the Quan clan and despised the Du.

sentences.zh: 及元禮至，與仲遵相見，感父臨別之言，潛與豪右結託。

translations.literal: When Yuanli arrived and met Zhongzun, moved by their father's parting words, they secretly joined with the powerful gentry in alliance.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanli returned and met Zhongzun, they were stirred by their father's farewell words and secretly won over the local leaders.

sentences.zh: 信宿之間，遂率鄉人襲州城，斬窋，傳首長安。

translations.literal: Within a night and a day they then led local men in a surprise attack on the provincial city, beheaded Qiong, and sent his head to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Within a day or two they led the local militia in a surprise attack on the capital, killed Qiong, and sent his head to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之，拜衛將軍、車騎大將軍，世襲洛州刺史。

translations.literal: The court praised them and appointed him Defender General and Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, with hereditary succession as Regional Inspector of Luo Province.
translations.idiomatic: The court commended them and made Yuanli defender general and grand general of chariots and cavalry, with the hereditary governorship of Luo.

sentences.zh: 從太祖戰於沙苑，為流矢所中，遂卒。

translations.literal: Following the Grand Progenitor in battle at Shayuan, he was struck by a stray arrow and thereupon died.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai at Shayuan, was struck by a stray arrow, and died.

sentences.zh: 子貞嗣，官至儀同三司。

translations.literal: His son Zhen succeeded him and reached the office of Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen inherited the line and rose to ceremonial parity with the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 仲遵少謹實，涉獵經史。

translations.literal: Zhongzun in youth was careful and sincere and ranged broadly through the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzun was careful and earnest from youth and read widely in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 年十三，州辟主簿。

translations.literal: At age thirteen the province summoned him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen the province recruited him as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 十四，為本縣令。

translations.literal: At fourteen he became magistrate of his home county.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he became magistrate of his home county.

sentences.zh: 及長，有武藝。

translations.literal: When he grew up he had martial skill.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he proved skilled in arms.

sentences.zh: 遭世離亂，每從父兄征討，以勇決聞。

translations.literal: Meeting an age of turmoil and disorder, he often followed his father and elder brothers on campaigns and was known for courage and resolution.
translations.idiomatic: In those troubled times he often campaigned with his father and brothers and won a name for bold decisiveness.

sentences.zh: 高敖曹攻洛州，企令仲遵率五百人出戰。

translations.literal: When Gao Aocao attacked Luo Province, Qi ordered Zhongzun to lead five hundred men out to battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Aocao attacked Luo, Qi sent Zhongzun out with five hundred men.

sentences.zh: 時以衆寡不敵，乃退入城，復與企力戰拒守。

translations.literal: At the time, because their numbers were few and could not match the enemy, they withdrew into the city and again with Qi fought strenuously in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing they were outnumbered, they fell back into the city and fought on beside Qi to hold the walls.

sentences.zh: 矢盡，以杖棒扞之，遂為流矢中目，不堪復戰。

translations.literal: When arrows were exhausted they used staffs and clubs to ward off the enemy; he was then struck in the eye by a stray arrow and could no longer fight.
translations.idiomatic: When the arrows ran out they beat back the assault with clubs; a stray shot struck him in the eye, and he could fight no more.

sentences.zh: 及城陷，士卒歎曰：「若二郎不傷，豈至於此。

translations.literal: When the city fell, the soldiers sighed: "If the Second Lord had not been wounded, how could it have come to this?
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell the soldiers said, "If the second son had not been wounded, we would never have come to this.

sentences.zh: 」企之東也，仲遵以被傷不行。

translations.literal: " When Qi went east, Zhongzun because of his wound did not go.
translations.idiomatic: " When Qi was taken east, Zhongzun stayed behind because of his wound.

sentences.zh: 後與元禮斬窋，以功封豐陽縣伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Later, together with Yuanli he beheaded Qiong; for his merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Fengyang County with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and Yuanli killed Qiong; for this he was enfeoffed baron of Fengyang with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 加授征東將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He was additionally given General Who Campaigns East and Regional Inspector of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made general who campaigns east and inspector of Yu.

sentences.zh: 及元禮於沙苑戰沒，復以仲遵為洛州刺史。

translations.literal: When Yuanli fell in battle at Shayuan, Zhongzun was again made Regional Inspector of Luo Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuanli's death at Shayuan, Zhongzun was appointed governor of Luo in his place.

sentences.zh: 仲遵宿稱幹略，為鄉里所歸。

translations.literal: Zhongzun had long been famed for capacity and strategy and was looked to by his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzun had long been known for ability and strategy and enjoyed the trust of his countrymen.

sentences.zh: 及為本州，頗得嘉譽。

translations.literal: When he governed his home province he won considerable praise.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of his home province he won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 東魏北豫州刺史高仲密舉成皋入附，太祖率軍應之，別遣仲遵隨于謹攻栢谷塢。

translations.literal: Gao Zhongmi, Regional Inspector of Northern Yu in Eastern Wei, raised Chenggao in submission; the Grand Progenitor led troops to respond, and separately sent Zhongzun with Yu Jin to attack the fortified stronghold of Baigu.
translations.idiomatic: When Eastern Wei's inspector of northern Yu, Gao Zhongmi, surrendered Chenggao, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai marched to support him and detached Zhongzun with Yu Jin to take the Baigu fort.

sentences.zh: 仲遵力戰先登，擒其將王顯明。

translations.literal: Zhongzun fought strenuously and was first to ascend, capturing their general Wang Xianming.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzun fought his way to the top first and captured the enemy general Wang Xianming.

sentences.zh: 栢谷旣拔，復會大軍戰於邙山。

translations.literal: Once Baigu was taken, he again joined the main army in battle at Mount Mang.
translations.idiomatic: After Baigu fell he rejoined the main army for the battle on Mount Mang.

sentences.zh: 十三年，王思政改鎮潁川，以仲遵行荊州刺史事。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Wang Sizheng was transferred to garrison Yingchuan, and Zhongzun was made to conduct the affairs of Regional Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Wang Sizheng was transferred to Yingchuan, and Zhongzun was put in charge of Jing province.

sentences.zh: 十五年，加授大都督，俄進車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was additionally made Chief Area Commander; soon he was advanced to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was made chief area commander, and soon promoted to grand general of chariots and cavalry with parity to the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 梁司州刺史柳仲禮每為邊寇，太祖令仲遵率鄉兵從開府楊忠討之。

translations.literal: Liu Zhongli, Regional Inspector of Si Province in Liang, repeatedly raided the border; the Grand Progenitor ordered Zhongzun to lead local troops following Baron Yang Zhong in campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's inspector of Si, Liu Zhongli, raided the frontier repeatedly; Grand Progenitor ordered Zhongzun to lead local troops under Yang Zhong against him.

sentences.zh: 梁隨郡守桓和拒守不降。

translations.literal: Huan He, Administrator of Sui Commandery in Liang, defended and would not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Huan He, Liang's administrator of Sui, held out and refused to surrender.

sentences.zh: 忠謂諸將曰：「本圖仲禮，不在隨郡。

translations.literal: Zhong said to the generals: "Our original plan was Zhongli, not Sui Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhong told his officers, "Our target is Zhongli, not Sui commandery.

sentences.zh: 如卽攻守，恐引日勞師。

translations.literal: If we immediately attack and defend, I fear it will draw out the days and weary the army.
translations.idiomatic: If we lay siege at once, I fear we will only weary the army day after day.

sentences.zh: 今若先取仲禮，則桓和可不攻自服。

translations.literal: If we now first take Zhongli, then Huan He may submit without attack.
translations.idiomatic: If we take Zhongli first, Huan He may surrender without a fight.

sentences.zh: 諸君以為何如？

translations.literal: What do you gentlemen think?
translations.idiomatic: What do you think?

sentences.zh: 」仲遵對曰：「蜂蠆有毒，何可輕也。

translations.literal: " Zhongzun replied: "Wasps and scorpions have poison—how can they be treated lightly?
translations.idiomatic: " Zhongzun answered, "Even wasps and scorpions have a sting—how can we take the enemy lightly?

sentences.zh: 若棄和深入，遂擒仲禮，和之降不，尚未可知。

translations.literal: If we abandon He and penetrate deeply, then capture Zhongli, whether He will submit is not yet knowable.
translations.idiomatic: If we leave Huan He and push deep inland to seize Zhongli, we cannot even be sure Huan He will submit.

sentences.zh: 如仲禮未獲，和為之援，首尾受敵，此危道也。

translations.literal: If Zhongli is not taken and He aids him, we will be attacked at head and tail—this is a perilous course.
translations.idiomatic: If we fail to take Zhongli while Huan He supports him from behind, we will be caught between two foes—that is a dangerous course.

sentences.zh: 若先攻和，指麾可剋。

translations.literal: If we first attack He, at a gesture he can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: If we strike Huan He first, he can be taken at a word.

sentences.zh: 剋和而進，更無反顧之憂。

translations.literal: Once He is taken and we advance, there will be no further worry of looking back.
translations.idiomatic: Once Huan He falls, we can advance with nothing at our backs.

sentences.zh: 」忠從之。

translations.literal: " Zhong followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Zhong agreed.

sentences.zh: 仲遵以計由己出，乃率先登城，遂擒和。

translations.literal: Because the plan came from himself, Zhongzun was first to ascend the wall and thereupon captured He.
translations.idiomatic: Since the plan was his own, Zhongzun was first up the wall and took Huan He.

sentences.zh: 仍從忠擊仲禮，又獲之。

translations.literal: He then followed Zhong in attacking Zhongli and captured him as well.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Yang Zhong against Liu Zhongli and captured him too.

sentences.zh: 進驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，領本州大中正，復為三荊二廣南雍平信江隨二郢淅等十三州諸軍事，行荊州刺史。

translations.literal: He was advanced to General of Agile Cavalry and Baron with an Establishment Equal to the Three Dukes, concurrently held chief rectifier of his home province, and again made commander-in-chief of military affairs of thirteen provinces including the Three Jing, Two Guang, Southern Yong, Ping, Xin, Jiang, Sui, Two Ying, Xi, and the rest, acting Regional Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general of agile cavalry with an open office equal to the three dukes, made chief rectifier of his home province, and again given command over thirteen provinces—Jing, Guang, Yong, and the rest—while serving as acting inspector of Jing.

sentences.zh: 尋遭母憂，請終喪制，不許。

translations.literal: Soon he encountered mourning for his mother and requested to complete the full mourning period; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He soon lost his mother and asked to observe full mourning, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 大將軍王雄南征上津、魏興，仲遵率所部兵從雄討平之。

translations.literal: Grand General Wang Xiong campaigned south against Shangjin and Weixing; Zhongzun led his own troops following Xiong to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Grand general Wang Xiong marched south against Shangjin and Weixing, and Zhongzun led his troops with him to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 遂於上津置南洛州，以仲遵為刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon at Shangjin they established Southern Luo Province, with Zhongzun as regional inspector.
translations.idiomatic: They then established Southern Luo province at Shangjin and made Zhongzun its inspector.

sentences.zh: 仲遵留情撫接，百姓安之，流民歸附者，相繼而至。

translations.literal: Zhongzun treated people with care and kindness; the common people were at ease, and displaced persons who came to attach themselves arrived one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzun governed with care and kindness; the people were at peace, and refugees kept arriving to settle under him.

sentences.zh: 初，蠻帥杜清和自稱巴州刺史，以州入附。

translations.literal: Earlier, the barbarian chieftain Du Qinghe had styled himself Regional Inspector of Ba Province and submitted the province in allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Man chieftain Du Qinghe had styled himself governor of Ba and surrendered the province.

sentences.zh: 朝廷因其所據授之，仍隸東梁州都督。

translations.literal: The court, according to the territory he held, appointed him to it, and he remained under the area commander of Eastern Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: The court recognized his holdings and appointed him, leaving him under the eastern Liang area commander.

sentences.zh: 清和以仲遵善於撫御，請隸仲遵。

translations.literal: Qinghe, because Zhongzun was skilled at pacification and control, requested to be placed under Zhongzun.
translations.idiomatic: Qinghe asked to be transferred to Zhongzun's jurisdiction because Zhongzun was skilled at governing the tribes.

sentences.zh: 朝議以山川非便，弗之許也。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that the mountains and rivers were inconvenient, and this was not approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court judged the terrain impractical and refused.

sentences.zh: 清和遂結安康酋帥黃衆寶等，舉兵共圍東梁州。

translations.literal: Qinghe thereupon joined with the Ankang chieftain Huang Zhongbao and others, raised troops, and together besieged Eastern Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Qinghe then allied with the Ankang chieftain Huang Zhongbao and others, took up arms, and besieged eastern Liang together.

sentences.zh: 復遣王雄討平之。

translations.literal: Wang Xiong was again sent to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiong was sent again and put down the revolt.

sentences.zh: 改巴州為洵州，隸於仲遵。

translations.literal: Ba Province was changed to Xun Province and placed under Zhongzun.
translations.idiomatic: Ba was renamed Xun and placed under Zhongzun.

sentences.zh: 先是，東梁州刺史劉孟良在職貪婪，民多背叛。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liu Mengliang, Regional Inspector of Eastern Liang, while in office was greedy; many of the people rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liu Mengliang, inspector of eastern Liang, had governed greedily and driven many people to revolt.

sentences.zh: 仲遵以廉簡處之，羣蠻率服。

translations.literal: Zhongzun governed with integrity and simplicity; the barbarian masses all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzun governed with integrity and simplicity, and the tribes submitted in full.

sentences.zh: 仲遵雖出自巴夷，而有方雅之操，歷官之處，皆以清白見稱。

translations.literal: Although Zhongzun came from Ba barbarian stock, he had the conduct of a man of proper elegance; in every office he held he was praised for integrity and purity.
translations.idiomatic: Though Zhongzun came from Ba tribal stock, he bore himself with proper dignity and was known everywhere for clean government.

sentences.zh: 朝廷又以其父臨危抗節，乃令襲爵上洛郡公，舊封聽回授一子。

translations.literal: The court also because his father at a crisis had upheld integrity, ordered him to succeed to the rank of Duke of Shangluo Commandery, with the former fief permitted to be transferred back to one son.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father had held firm at the crisis, the court let him inherit the dukedom of Shangluo and allowed one son to receive his earlier fief in turn.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝初，徵拜左衛將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gong of Wei he was summoned and appointed Left Defender General.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Gong of Wei's reign he was summoned as left defender general.

sentences.zh: 尋出為都督金興等六州諸軍事、金州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as area commander of military affairs of six provinces including Jin and Xing, and Regional Inspector of Jin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent out as commander of six provinces including Jin and Xing and inspector of Jin.

sentences.zh: 武成初，卒官，時年四十五。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wucheng he died in office, aged forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wucheng era he died in office at forty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈大將軍、華洛等三州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Grand General and Regional Inspector of the three provinces Hua, Luo, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand general and inspector of Hua, Luo, and two other provinces.

sentences.zh: 諡曰莊。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子端嗣。

translations.literal: His son Duan succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Duan inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 起家本縣令，入為左侍上士。

translations.literal: He began his career as magistrate of his home county, entered service as Left Attendant Senior Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He began as magistrate of his home county and entered court as left attendant senior gentleman.

sentences.zh: 保定中，授帥都督，累遷儀同三司，出為純州防主。

translations.literal: In the Baoding era he was given the rank of commander-in-chief, was repeatedly promoted to Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, and went out as defense commander of Chun Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding he was made a commander-in-chief, rose to ceremonial parity with the three dukes, and became defense commander of Chun.

sentences.zh: 建德末，位至開府儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Jiande he reached the rank of Grand General with an Establishment Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Jiande he had risen to grand general with an open office equal to the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 李遷哲字孝彥，安康人也。

translations.literal: Li Qianzhe, courtesy name Xiaoyan, was a native of Ankang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qianzhe, courtesy name Xiaoyan, came from Ankang.

sentences.zh: 世為山南豪族，仕於江左。

translations.literal: For generations his clan had been a powerful family south of the mountains, serving in the Jiang left.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family had been a great clan south of the mountains and had served the southern dynasties.

sentences.zh: 祖方達，齊末，為本州治中。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fangda, at the end of Qi, was chief clerk of his home province.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fangda, late in Qi, had been chief clerk of their home province.

sentences.zh: 父元真，仕梁，歷東宮左衛率、東梁衡二州刺史、散騎常侍、沌陽侯。

translations.literal: His father Yuanzhen served Liang, successively holding Eastern Palace Left Commandant of the Guard, Regional Inspector of the two provinces Eastern Liang and Heng, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and Marquis of Zhunyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuanzhen served Liang as eastern-palace left commandant of the guard, inspector of eastern Liang and Heng, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, and marquis of Zhunyang.

sentences.zh: 遷哲少修立，有識度，慷慨善謀畫。

translations.literal: Qianzhe in youth cultivated himself and was upright, had discernment and breadth, was generous and skilled in planning.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Qianzhe was upright and self-disciplined, far-sighted and generous, and skilled in strategy.

sentences.zh: 起家文德主帥，轉直閤將軍、武賁中郎將。

translations.literal: He began his career as commander of Wende, was transferred to Direct Palace General and Majestic Guard Central Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a Wende commander, then became a direct-palace general and majestic-guard central commandant.

sentences.zh: 及其父為衡州，留遷哲本鄉，監統部曲事。

translations.literal: When his father was at Heng Province, Qianzhe was left in his home district to supervise and command the household troops.
translations.idiomatic: When his father went to Heng province, Qianzhe remained at home to command the family forces.

sentences.zh: 時年二十，撫馭羣下，甚得其情。

translations.literal: At the time he was twenty years old; in comforting and controlling his subordinates he won their hearts extremely well.
translations.idiomatic: Though only twenty, he won his followers' loyalty completely.

sentences.zh: 大同二年，除安康郡守。

translations.literal: In the second year of Datong he was appointed Administrator of Ankang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Datong he was made administrator of Ankang.

sentences.zh: 三年，加超武將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year he was additionally made Transcendent Martial General.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made transcendent martial general.

sentences.zh: 太清二年，移鎮魏興郡，都督魏興、上庸等八郡諸軍事，襲爵沌陽侯，邑一千五百戶。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiqing he was transferred to garrison Weixing Commandery, area commander of military affairs of eight commanderies including Weixing and Shangyong, succeeded to the rank of Marquis of Zhunyang, fief of one thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiqing he was posted to Weixing, given command over eight commanderies, and inherited the marquisate of Zhunyang with fifteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷持節、信武將軍、散騎常侍、都督東梁洵興等七州諸軍事、東梁州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to credential-holder, Trustworthy Martial General, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, area commander of military affairs of seven provinces including Eastern Liang, Xun, and Xing, and Regional Inspector of Eastern Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he received credentials, the rank of trustworthy martial general and regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, command over seven provinces, and the governorship of eastern Liang.

sentences.zh: 及侯景篡逆，諸王爭帝，遷哲外禦邊寇，自守而已。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing usurped and rebelled and the princes contended for the throne, Qianzhe outwardly resisted border enemies and merely held his ground.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled and the princes fought for the throne, Qianzhe held his ground and merely defended the frontier.

sentences.zh: 大統十七年，太祖遣達奚武、王雄等略地山南，遷哲率其所部拒戰，軍敗，遂降于武。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Datong the Grand Progenitor sent Daxi Wu, Wang Xiong, and others to seize territory south of the mountains; Qianzhe led his forces to resist, the army was defeated, and he thereupon surrendered to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Datong Grand Progenitor sent Daxi Wu and Wang Xiong to seize the mountain south; Qianzhe resisted, was defeated, and surrendered to Wu.

sentences.zh: 然猶意氣自若。

translations.literal: Yet his spirit and bearing were still as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he remained as composed as ever.

sentences.zh: 武乃執送京師。

translations.literal: Wu then seized him and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wu then sent him to the capital under guard.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂之曰：「何不早歸國家，乃勞師旅。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said to him: "Why did you not submit to the state earlier, and thus weary the army?
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor said to him, "Why did you not submit earlier and spare us this campaign?

sentences.zh: 今為俘虜，不亦愧乎？

translations.literal: Now as a captive, is it not shameful?
translations.idiomatic: Now that you are a prisoner, are you not ashamed?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「世荷梁恩，未有報效，又不能死節，實以此為愧耳。

translations.literal: " He replied: "For generations I have received Liang's grace and have had no way to repay it; moreover I could not die for the cause—this is what I am ashamed of.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "My family owed Liang a debt I never repaid, and I could not die for the cause—that is my shame.

sentences.zh: 」太祖深嘉之，卽拜使持節、車騎大將軍、散騎常侍，封沌陽縣伯，邑千戶。

translations.literal: " The Grand Progenitor deeply praised him and at once appointed him Envoy Holding Credentials, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, enfeoffed as Baron of Zhunyang County with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Progenitor admired him greatly and at once made him envoy with credentials, grand general of chariots and cavalry, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, and baron of Zhunyang with a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝初，直州人樂熾、洋州人田越、金州人黃國等連結為亂。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gong of Wei, the men of Zhi Province Le Chi, the men of Yang Province Tian Yue, the men of Jin Province Huang Guo, and others joined in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Gong of Wei's reign Le Chi of Zhi, Tian Yue of Yang, Huang Guo of Jin, and others rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣鴈門公田弘出梁漢，開府賀若敦趣直谷。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor sent the Duke of Yanmen Tian Hong out through Liang and Han, and Baron Heluo Dun hastened to Zhigu.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor sent Duke of Yanmen Tian Hong through Liang and Han and baron Heluo Dun toward Zhigu.

sentences.zh: 熾聞官軍至，乃燒絕棧道，據守直谷，敦衆不得前。

translations.literal: When Chi heard the government army had arrived, he burned and cut the plank roads, held Zhigu, and Dun's forces could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When Chi heard the government troops were coming, he burned the plank roads and held Zhigu, blocking Dun's advance.

sentences.zh: 太祖以遷哲信著山南，乃令與敦同往經略。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor, because Qianzhe's trustworthiness was well known south of the mountains, ordered him to go with Dun on the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Because Qianzhe was trusted throughout the mountain south, Grand Progenitor sent him with Dun on the campaign.

sentences.zh: 熾等或降或獲，尋竝平蕩。

translations.literal: Chi and the others either submitted or were captured; soon all were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Chi and the rest either surrendered or were captured, and the region was soon pacified.

sentences.zh: 仍與賀若敦南出狥地。

translations.literal: He then with Heluo Dun marched south to seize territory.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched south with Heluo Dun to seize more territory.

sentences.zh: 遷哲先至巴州，入其郛郭。

translations.literal: Qianzhe arrived first at Ba Province and entered its outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhe reached Ba first and entered its outer city.

sentences.zh: 梁巴州刺史牟安民惶懼，開門請降。

translations.literal: Liang's Regional Inspector of Ba Province Mou Anmin was fearful and opened the gate to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's Ba inspector Mou Anmin, in terror, opened the gates and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 安民子宗徹等猶據琵琶城，招諭不下。

translations.literal: Anmin's son Zongche and others still held Pipa walled city and would not submit though summoned and instructed.
translations.idiomatic: Anmin's son Zongche still held Pipa city and would not yield despite appeals.

sentences.zh: 遷哲攻而克之，斬獲九百餘人。

translations.literal: Qianzhe attacked and took it, beheading and capturing more than nine hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhe stormed it, killing and capturing more than nine hundred men.

sentences.zh: 軍次鹿城，城主遣使請降。

translations.literal: The army halted at Lucheng; the city lord sent envoys to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At Lucheng the city lord sent envoys offering surrender.

sentences.zh: 遷哲謂其衆曰：「納降如受敵，吾觀其使視瞻猶高，得無詐也？

translations.literal: Qianzhe said to his troops: "To accept surrender is like facing an enemy; I see their envoy's gaze is still high—could there not be deception?
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhe told his men, "Accepting surrender is like meeting an enemy; that envoy's eyes are still proud—could this be a trap?

sentences.zh: 」遂不許之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: " He refused the offer.

sentences.zh: 梁人果於道左設伏以邀遷哲，遷哲進擊，破之，遂屠其城，虜獲千餘口。

translations.literal: The men of Liang indeed set an ambush on the left of the road to intercept Qianzhe; Qianzhe advanced to attack and defeated them, then slaughtered their city, capturing more than a thousand mouths.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang forces had indeed set an ambush; Qianzhe attacked, broke them, sacked the city, and took more than a thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 自此巴、濮之民，降款相繼。

translations.literal: From this time the people of Ba and Pu submitted in succession.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the people of Ba and Pu submitted one after another.

sentences.zh: 軍還，太祖嘉之，以所服紫袍玉帶及所乘馬以賜之，並賜奴婢三十口。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the Grand Progenitor praised him and gave him the purple robe and jade belt he wore and the horse he rode, and also bestowed thirty household slaves.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Grand Progenitor praised him, gave him his own purple robe, jade belt, and horse, and thirty household slaves.

sentences.zh: 加授侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，除直州刺史，卽本州也。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, and Baron with an Establishment Equal to the Three Dukes, appointed Regional Inspector of Zhi Province—that is, his home province.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made palace attendant, general of agile cavalry, and baron with an open office equal to the three dukes, and appointed inspector of Zhi—his home province.

sentences.zh: 仍給軍儀鼓節。

translations.literal: He was also given military drums, banners, and credentials.
translations.idiomatic: He was also given military drums, banners, and credentials.

sentences.zh: 令與田弘同討信州。

translations.literal: He was ordered to campaign against Xin Province together with Tian Hong.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to join Tian Hong in the campaign against Xin.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝三年正月，軍次并州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Emperor Gong of Wei the army halted at Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year of Emperor Gong of Wei the army reached Bing province.

sentences.zh: 梁并州刺史杜滿各望風送款。

translations.literal: Liang's Regional Inspector of Bing Province Du Man and others submitted upon seeing the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's Bing inspector Du Man and others surrendered at the first approach.

sentences.zh: 進圍疊州，克之，獲刺史冉助國等。

translations.literal: They advanced to besiege Die Province, took it, and captured the regional inspector Ran Zhuguo and others.
translations.idiomatic: They advanced to besiege Die, took it, and captured inspector Ran Zhuguo and others.

sentences.zh: 遷哲每率驍勇為前鋒，所在攻戰，無不身先士卒，凡下十八州，拓地三千餘里。

translations.literal: Qianzhe each time led the fierce warriors as vanguard; wherever he attacked and fought there was none in which he did not personally lead the troops from the front; in all he reduced eighteen provinces and extended territory more than three thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhe always led the assault himself; in eighteen provinces and three thousand li of conquered territory he was always first in the fight.

sentences.zh: 時信州為蠻酋向五子王等所圍，弘又遣遷哲赴援。

translations.literal: At the time Xin Province was besieged by the barbarian chieftains Xiang Wuzi Wang and others; Hong again sent Qianzhe to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was then besieged by the Man chieftains Xiang Wuzi Wang and others, and Hong sent Qianzhe to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 比至，信州已陷。

translations.literal: By the time he arrived, Xin Province had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he arrived, Xin had already fallen.

sentences.zh: 五子王等聞遷哲至，狼狽遁走。

translations.literal: Wuzi Wang and the others, hearing Qianzhe had come, fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzi Wang and the others fled in panic when they heard Qianzhe was coming.

sentences.zh: 遷哲入據白帝。

translations.literal: Qianzhe entered and occupied Baidi.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhe entered and occupied Baidi.

sentences.zh: 賀若敦等復至，遂共追擊五子王等，破之。

translations.literal: Heluo Dun and the others also arrived, and together they pursued and attacked Wuzi Wang and the others and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Heluo Dun arrived as well, and together they pursued and defeated Wuzi Wang.

sentences.zh: 及田弘旋軍，太祖令遷哲留鎮白帝，更配兵千人、馬三百匹。

translations.literal: When Tian Hong turned the army, the Grand Progenitor ordered Qianzhe to remain and garrison Baidi, additionally assigning him one thousand troops and three hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Hong withdrew, Grand Progenitor left Qianzhe to garrison Baidi with another thousand troops and three hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 信州先無倉儲，軍糧匱乏。

translations.literal: Xin Province had had no granaries earlier; army provisions were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Xin had no granaries, and army provisions ran short.

sentences.zh: 遷哲乃收葛根造粉，兼米以給之。

translations.literal: Qianzhe then gathered kudzu roots to make flour and mixed it with rice to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhe gathered kudzu roots to make flour and mixed it with rice to feed the troops.

sentences.zh: 遷哲亦自取供食。

translations.literal: Qianzhe also took his own provisions.
translations.idiomatic: He lived on the same fare himself.

sentences.zh: 時有異膳，卽分賜兵士。

translations.literal: When there was special food he at once divided and bestowed it on the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever there was special food he shared it with the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 有疾患者，又親加醫藥。

translations.literal: When there were sick men he personally gave them medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When men fell ill he tended them himself.

sentences.zh: 以此軍中感之，人思效命。

translations.literal: Because of this the army was moved by him and every man wished to devote his life.
translations.idiomatic: The army was deeply moved, and every man was ready to die for him.

sentences.zh: 黔陽蠻田烏度、田都唐等每抄掠江中，為百姓患。

translations.literal: The Qianyang barbarians Tian Wudu, Tian Dutang, and others repeatedly raided the river and were a calamity to the common people.
translations.idiomatic: The Qianyang Man Tian Wudu and Tian Dutang raided the river country and plagued the people.

sentences.zh: 遷哲隨機出討，殺獲甚多。

translations.literal: Qianzhe went out to attack them as opportunity arose and killed and captured a great many.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhe struck whenever opportunity offered and killed or captured many.

sentences.zh: 由是諸蠻畏威，各送糧餼。

translations.literal: Because of this the various barbarians feared his might and each sent grain provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes feared him and sent grain tribute.

sentences.zh: 又遣子弟入質者，千有餘家。

translations.literal: Those who sent sons and younger brothers in as hostages numbered more than a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand families sent sons as hostages.

sentences.zh: 遷哲乃於白帝城外築城以處之。

translations.literal: Qianzhe then built a city outside Baidi to house them.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhe built a city outside Baidi to house them.

sentences.zh: 並置四鎮，以靜峽路。

translations.literal: He also established four garrisons to quiet the Gorges route.
translations.idiomatic: He also set up four garrisons to secure the Gorges route.

sentences.zh: 自此寇抄頗息，軍糧贍給焉。

translations.literal: From this time raiding and plundering largely ceased, and army provisions were supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Raids largely ceased, and army provisions were assured.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，授都督信臨等七州諸軍事、信州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizong he was appointed area commander of military affairs of seven provinces including Xin and Lin, and Regional Inspector of Xin Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Shizong's reign he was made commander of seven provinces including Xin and Lin and inspector of Xin.

sentences.zh: 時蠻酋蒲微為鄰州刺史，舉兵反。

translations.literal: At the time the barbarian chieftain Pu Wei was Regional Inspector of a neighboring province and raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Man chieftain Pu Wei, inspector of a neighboring province, rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 遷哲將討之，諸將以途路阻遠，竝不欲行。

translations.literal: Qianzhe was about to campaign against him; the generals all held that the roads were blocked and far, and none wished to go.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhe prepared to campaign against him, but his officers objected that the route was long and difficult.

sentences.zh: 遷哲怒曰：「蒲微蕞爾之賊，勢何能為。

translations.literal: Qianzhe said angrily: "Pu Wei is a trifling bandit—what power can he have?
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhe said angrily, "Pu Wei is a petty rebel—what can he do?

sentences.zh: 擒獲之略，已在吾度中矣。

translations.literal: The plan to capture him is already within my reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: I already know how to take him.

sentences.zh: 諸君見此小寇，便有憚心，後遇大敵，將何以戰！

translations.literal: You gentlemen see this small bandit and already have fear in your hearts—later when you meet a great enemy, how will you fight!
translations.idiomatic: If you shrink from this little foe, how will you fight when a real enemy comes!

sentences.zh: 」遂率兵七千人進擊之，拔其五城，虜獲二千餘口。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he led seven thousand troops to attack him, took five of his cities, and captured more than two thousand mouths.
translations.idiomatic: " He then led seven thousand men against him, took five cities, and captured more than two thousand people.

sentences.zh: 二年，進爵西城縣公，增邑通前二千五百戶。

translations.literal: In the second year his rank was advanced to Duke of Xicheng County, with fief households increased together with earlier holdings to two thousand five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was raised to duke of Xicheng, his fief increased to twenty-five hundred households in all.

sentences.zh: 武成元年，朝于京師。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wucheng he attended court at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wucheng he went to court at the capital.

sentences.zh: 世宗甚禮之，賜甲第一區及莊田等。

translations.literal: Shizong treated him with great courtesy and bestowed a first-rank residence and manor fields and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong received him with great honor and gave him a first-rank mansion, manor lands, and more.

sentences.zh: 保定中，授平州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Baoding era he was appointed Regional Inspector of Ping Province.
translations.idiomatic: During Baoding he was made inspector of Ping.

sentences.zh: 天和三年，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhe he was advanced to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianhe he was promoted to grand general.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔遷哲率金、上等諸州兵鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: In the fourth year an edict ordered Qianzhe to lead troops of Jin, Shang, and other provinces to garrison Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was ordered to lead troops from Jin, Shang, and other provinces to garrison Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 五年，陳將章昭達攻逼江陵。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Chen general Zhang Zhaoda pressed Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the Chen general Zhang Zhaoda besieged Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 梁主蕭巋告急於襄州，衛公直令遷哲往救焉。

translations.literal: The Liang ruler Xiao Kui urgently reported to Xiang Province; Duke of Wei Yang Zhi ordered Qianzhe to go to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang ruler Xiao Kui appealed to Xiang province for help, and Duke of Wei Yang Zhi sent Qianzhe to relieve Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 遷哲率其所部守江陵外城，與陳將程文季交戰，兵稍卻，遷哲乃親自陷陣，手殺數人。

translations.literal: Qianzhe led his own forces to defend the outer wall of Jiangling and fought with the Chen general Cheng Wenji; his troops gradually fell back, and Qianzhe then personally broke into the formation and with his own hand killed several men.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhe held the outer wall of Jiangling and fought Cheng Wenji; when his men gave ground he plunged into the battle himself and killed several foes.

sentences.zh: 會江陵總管陸騰出助之，陳人乃退。

translations.literal: When Jiangling headquarters commander Lu Teng came out to assist, the Chen men then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When headquarters commander Lu Teng came to his aid, the Chen forces withdrew.

sentences.zh: 陳人又因水泛長，壞龍川寧朔堤，引水灌城。

translations.literal: The Chen men also took advantage of the swollen waters, destroyed the Longchuan and Ningshuo dikes, and led water to flood the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen army broke the Longchuan and Ningshuo dikes and flooded the city.

sentences.zh: 城中驚擾。

translations.literal: Within the city there was alarm and disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: Panic spread through the city.

sentences.zh: 遷哲乃先塞北堤以止水，又募驍勇出擊之，頻有斬獲，衆心稍定。

translations.literal: Qianzhe then first blocked the northern dike to stop the water, and also recruited fierce warriors to sally out and attack them; he frequently had beheadings and captures, and the hearts of the masses gradually settled.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhe first sealed the northern dike to stop the flood, then sent picked troops out to strike; after several successes the people steadied.

sentences.zh: 俄而敵入郭內，焚燒民家。

translations.literal: Soon the enemy entered within the outer wall and burned the houses of the people.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the enemy broke into the suburbs and burned civilian houses.

sentences.zh: 遷哲自率騎出南門，又令步兵自北門出，兩軍合勢，首尾邀之，陳人復敗，多投水而死。

translations.literal: Qianzhe himself led cavalry out through the south gate and also ordered infantry out through the north gate; the two armies combined their strength and attacked head and tail, and the Chen men were defeated again, many throwing themselves into the water to die.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhe led cavalry out the south gate and infantry out the north, caught the Chen army between two forces, and routed it; many drowned fleeing into the water.

sentences.zh: 是夜，陳人又竊於城西堞以梯〔登城〕，登者已數百人。

translations.literal: That night the Chen men again secretly used ladders on the western battlements to 〔ascend the wall〕; those who had climbed numbered already several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: That night the Chen tried to scale the western wall with ladders; several hundred men had already climbed up.

sentences.zh: 遷哲又率驍勇扞之，陳人復潰。

translations.literal: Qianzhe again led fierce warriors to ward them off, and the Chen men again collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhe led picked troops against them and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 俄而大風暴起，遷哲乘闇出兵擊其營，陳人大亂，殺傷甚衆。

translations.literal: Soon a great windstorm arose; Qianzhe took advantage of the darkness to send troops out to attack their camp, and the Chen men fell into great disorder with many killed and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: A violent storm arose; Qianzhe struck their camp in the dark and threw the Chen army into chaos with heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 陸騰復破之於西堤，陳人乃遁。

translations.literal: Lu Teng again defeated them at the western dike, and the Chen men then fled.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Teng defeated them again at the western dike, and the Chen army fled.

sentences.zh: 建德二年，進爵安康郡公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiande his rank was advanced to Duke of Ankang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiande he was raised to duke of Ankang.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒於襄州，時年六十四。

translations.literal: In the third year he died at Xiang Province, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he died at Xiangyang at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈金州總管。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given headquarters commander of Jin Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made headquarters commander of Jin.

sentences.zh: 諡曰壯武。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Zhuangwu.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Zhuangwu.

sentences.zh: 遷哲累世雄豪，為鄉里所率服。

translations.literal: Qianzhe for generations had been powerful and heroic and was followed and submitted to by his home district.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the Qianzhe clan had been powerful locally and commanded the district's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 性復華侈，能厚自奉養。

translations.literal: His nature was again luxurious; he could richly provide for himself.
translations.idiomatic: He was also lavish by nature and lived in great style.

sentences.zh: 妾媵至有百數，男女六十九人。

translations.literal: His concubines reached a hundred in number; his sons and daughters numbered sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He had as many as a hundred concubines and sixty-nine children.

sentences.zh: 緣漢千餘里間，第宅相次。

translations.literal: Along more than a thousand li of the Han River, mansions followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: For more than a thousand li along the Han he had estate after estate.

sentences.zh: 姬人之有子者，分處其中，各有僮僕、侍婢、奄閽守之。

translations.literal: Among his consorts who had sons, each was placed in one of them, each with her own servants, maids, and eunuch guards.
translations.idiomatic: Each concubine who bore a son had her own house, with servants, maids, and eunuch guards.

sentences.zh: 遷哲每鳴笳導從，往來其間。

translations.literal: Qianzhe each time sounded the horn and led his retinue, going back and forth among them.
translations.idiomatic: He would sound his horn and ride with a great retinue from one house to the next.

sentences.zh: 縱酒飲燕，盡生平之樂。

translations.literal: He would set out wine and hold banquets, exhausting the pleasures of his life.
translations.idiomatic: There he feasted and drank his fill, enjoying every pleasure life could offer.

sentences.zh: 子孫參見，或忘其年名者，披簿以審之。

translations.literal: When sons and grandsons came to see him, he sometimes forgot their years and names and opened the register to verify.
translations.idiomatic: When sons and grandsons visited, he sometimes forgot their names and ages and had to check the family register.

sentences.zh: 長子敬仁，先遷哲卒。

translations.literal: His eldest son Jingren died before Qianzhe.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Jingren died before he did.

sentences.zh: 第六子敬猷嗣，還統父兵，起家大都督。

translations.literal: His sixth son Jingyou succeeded, again commanding his father's troops, and began his career as Chief Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth son Jingyou inherited the line, took command of his father's troops, and began as chief area commander.

sentences.zh: 建德六年，從譙王討稽胡有功，進爵儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiande he followed the Prince of Qiao in campaigning against the Jiehu with merit and was advanced in rank to Grand General Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Jiande he campaigned against the Jiehu under the Prince of Qiao and was raised to grand general equal to the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 遷哲弟顯，位至上儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: Qianzhe's younger brother Xian reached the office of Senior Grand General Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhe's younger brother Xian rose to senior grand general equal to the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 楊乾運字玄邈，儻城興勢人也。

translations.literal: Yang Ganyun, courtesy name Xuanmiao, was a native of Xingshi in Tangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ganyun, courtesy name Xuanmiao, came from Xingshi in Tangcheng.

sentences.zh: 為方隅豪族。

translations.literal: He was a powerful clan of the border region.
translations.idiomatic: His clan was powerful in the borderlands.

sentences.zh: 父天興，齊安康郡守。

translations.literal: His father Tianxing was Administrator of Ankang Commandery under Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tianxing had been administrator of Ankang under Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 乾運少雄武，為鄉閭所信服。

translations.literal: Ganyun in youth was fierce and martial and was trusted and believed by his home district.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Ganyun was bold and martial and trusted by his countrymen.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，州辟主簿。

translations.literal: At the capping ceremony the province summoned him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: At his capping the province recruited him as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，除宣威將軍、奉朝請，尋為本州治中，轉別駕，除安康郡守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang he was appointed General of Manifest Might and Court Gentleman for the Imperial Audience; soon he was made chief clerk of his home province, transferred to vice director, and appointed Administrator of Ankang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiaochang he became general of manifest might and court gentleman, then chief clerk and vice director of his province, and administrator of Ankang.

sentences.zh: 大統初，梁州民皇甫圓、姜晏聚衆南叛，梁將蘭欽率兵應接之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong the people of Liang Province Huangfu Yuan and Jiang Yan gathered crowds and rebelled southward; the Liang general Lan Qin led troops to meet and support them.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Datong, Huangfu Yuan and Jiang Yan of Liang province rebelled, and the Liang general Lan Qin marched to support them.

sentences.zh: 以是漢中遂陷，乾運亦入梁。

translations.literal: Because of this Hanzhong then fell, and Ganyun also entered Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhong fell, and Ganyun went over to Liang as well.

sentences.zh: 梁大同元年，除飄武將軍、西益潼刺史，尋轉信武將軍、黎州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong of Liang he was appointed Drifting Martial General and Regional Inspector of Xi, Yi, and Tong, and soon transferred to Trustworthy Martial General and Regional Inspector of Li Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang's first year of Datong he was made drifting martial general and inspector of Xi, Yi, and Tong, then trustworthy martial general and inspector of Li.

sentences.zh: 太清末，遷潼南梁二州刺史，加鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: At the end of Taiqing he was transferred to Regional Inspector of the two provinces Tong and Liang, with one set of martial music added.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Taiqing he became inspector of Tong and Liang, with a military band added to his retinue.

sentences.zh: 及達奚武圍南鄭，武陵王蕭紀遣乾運率兵援之，為武所敗。

translations.literal: When Daxi Wu besieged Nanzheng, the Prince of Wuling Xiao Ji sent Ganyun to lead troops to relieve it and he was defeated by Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When Daxi Wu besieged Nanzheng, Prince of Wuling Xiao Ji sent Ganyun to relieve the city, but Wu defeated him.

sentences.zh: 紀時已稱尊號，以乾運威服巴、渝，欲委方面之任，乃拜車騎將軍、十三州諸軍事、梁州刺史，鎮潼州，封萬春縣公，邑四千戶。

translations.literal: Ji had already styled himself with an exalted title; because Ganyun's might had subdued Ba and Yu, he wished to entrust him with a frontier command, and thus appointed him Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, commander-in-chief of military affairs of thirteen provinces, Regional Inspector of Liang Province, garrisoning Tong Province, enfeoffed as Duke of Wanchun County with a fief of four thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had already declared himself emperor; because Ganyun commanded Ba and Yu, he made him grand general of chariots and cavalry, commander of thirteen provinces, inspector of Liang, with his seat at Tong, and duke of Wanchun with four thousand households.

sentences.zh: 時紀與其兄湘東王繹爭帝，遂連兵不息。

translations.literal: At the time Ji and his elder brother the Prince of Xiangdong Xiao Yi contended for the throne, and thus warfare between them did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was then fighting his brother Xiao Yi of Xiangdong for the throne, and the war dragged on.

sentences.zh: 乾運兄子畧說乾運曰：「自侯景逆亂，江左沸騰。

translations.literal: Ganyun's nephew Lue said to Ganyun: "Since Hou Jing's rebellion the Jiang left has boiled and seethed.
translations.idiomatic: Ganyun's nephew Lue said to him, "Since Hou Jing rebelled the lower Yangzi has been in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 今大賊初平，生民離散，理宜同心戮力，保國寧民。

translations.literal: Now the great bandit is newly pacified, the living people are scattered and displaced—it is right that we should with one heart join our strength to preserve the state and bring peace to the people.
translations.idiomatic: The great rebellion is barely over and the people are scattered—we ought to unite and restore order.

sentences.zh: 今乃兄弟親尋。

translations.literal: Now yet brothers seek out one another in strife.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now these brothers turn on each other.

sentences.zh: 取敗之道也。

translations.literal: This is the way to invite defeat.
translations.idiomatic: That is the road to ruin.

sentences.zh: 可謂朽木不雕，世衰難佐。

translations.literal: One may say of rotten wood it cannot be carved; when the age declines it is hard to assist.
translations.idiomatic: As the saying goes, rotten wood cannot be carved, and a declining age is hard to serve.

sentences.zh: 古人有言『危邦不入，亂邦不居』，又云『見機而作，不俟終日』，今若適彼樂土，送款關中，必當功名兩全，貽慶於後。

translations.literal: The ancients had a saying, "Do not enter a state in peril, do not dwell in a state in disorder," and again, "When you see the moment, act—do not wait for the full day." If we now go to that happy land and offer our allegiance to Guanzhong, we shall surely achieve both fame and merit and leave blessings for those who come after.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, "Do not enter a perilous state or dwell in a chaotic one," and "Act when you see your chance." If we now submit to Guanzhong, we may win honor and leave blessings for our descendants.

sentences.zh: 」乾運深然之，乃令略將二千人鎮劔閣。

translations.literal: " Ganyun deeply approved this and thereupon ordered Lue to lead two thousand men to garrison Jiange.
translations.idiomatic: " Ganyun agreed and sent Lue with two thousand men to hold Jiange.

sentences.zh: 又遣其婿樂廣鎮安州。

translations.literal: He also sent his son-in-law Yue Guang to garrison An Province.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his son-in-law Yue Guang to hold An province.

sentences.zh: 仍誡畧等曰：「吾欲歸附關中，但未有由耳。

translations.literal: He still admonished Lue and the others: "I wish to submit to Guanzhong, but as yet have no means.
translations.idiomatic: He told Lue and the others, "I mean to submit to Guanzhong, but I still lack an opening.

sentences.zh: 若有使來，卽宜盡禮迎接。

translations.literal: If envoys come, you should at once receive them with full courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When envoys arrive, receive them with full courtesy.

sentences.zh: 」會太祖令乾運孫法洛及使人牛伯友等至，略卽夜送〔之〕。

translations.literal: " When the Grand Progenitor sent Ganyun's grandson Faluo and the envoy Niu Boyou and others to arrive, Lue that same night sent 〔them〕 on.
translations.idiomatic: " When Grand Progenitor sent his grandson Faluo and the envoy Niu Boyou, Lue forwarded them that same night.

sentences.zh: 乾運乃令使人李若等入關送款。

translations.literal: Ganyun then ordered the envoy Li Ruo and others to enter Guan and offer allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Ganyun then sent Li Ruo and others through the passes to offer submission.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃密賜乾運鐵券，授使持節、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、侍中、梁州刺史、安康郡公。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor then secretly bestowed on Ganyun an iron certificate, appointing him Envoy Holding Credentials, General of Agile Cavalry, Baron with an Establishment Equal to the Three Dukes, Palace Attendant, Regional Inspector of Liang Province, and Duke of Ankang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor secretly gave him an iron certificate and made him envoy with credentials, general of agile cavalry, baron with an open office equal to the three dukes, palace attendant, inspector of Liang, and duke of Ankang.

sentences.zh: 及尉遲迥令開府侯呂陵始為前軍，至劍南，略卽退就樂廣，謀欲翻城。

translations.literal: When Yu Chi Jiong ordered Baron Hou Lvling Shi to be the vanguard army and reach Jiannan, Lue then withdrew to join Yue Guang and plotted to turn the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Chi Jiong sent baron Hou Lvling Shi as vanguard to Jiannan, Lue fell back to Yue Guang and plotted to open the city.

sentences.zh: 恐其軍將任電等不同，先執之，然後出城見始。

translations.literal: Fearing that his military officers Ren Dian and others would not agree, he first seized them, and then went out of the city to see Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing his officers would not agree, he arrested Ren Dian and the others first, then went out to meet Shi.

sentences.zh: 始乃入據安州，令廣、略等往報乾運。

translations.literal: Shi then entered and occupied An Province and ordered Guang, Lue, and the others to go report to Ganyun.
translations.idiomatic: Shi entered An, then sent Guang and Lue to inform Ganyun.

sentences.zh: 乾運遂降迥。

translations.literal: Ganyun thereupon surrendered to Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Ganyun then surrendered to Jiong.

sentences.zh: 迥因此進軍成都，數旬尅之。

translations.literal: Jiong therefore advanced the army to Chengdu, and within several tens of days took it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong marched on Chengdu and took it within weeks.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝三年，乾運至京師。

translations.literal: In the third year of Emperor Fei of Wei, Ganyun reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Emperor Fei of Wei, Ganyun reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉其忠款，禮遇隆渥。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor praised his loyal submission and treated him with lofty courtesy and thick generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor praised his loyalty and received him with great honor.

sentences.zh: 尋卒於長安，贈本官，加直巴集三州刺史、尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Soon he died at Chang'an; he was given his former offices posthumously, additionally made Regional Inspector of the three provinces Zhi, Ba, and Ji, and Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died at Chang'an; his former offices were confirmed posthumously, with added posts as inspector of Zhi, Ba, and Ji and right vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子端嗣。

translations.literal: His son Duan succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Duan inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以乾運歸附之功，卽拜端梁州刺史、車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: The court, because of Ganyun's merit in submitting allegiance, at once appointed Duan Regional Inspector of Liang Province, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: For Ganyun's submission the court at once made Duan inspector of Liang, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and equal to the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 畧亦以歸附功，拜車騎大將軍、儀同三司。
